llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed research-wiki helper that writes local knowledge-base files and can optionally download arXiv PDFs, with some quality and consent-scope caveats but no evidence of deception or malicious behavior.

dimensions.detail: Local writes are scoped to research-wiki style paths such as raw/, wiki/, and assets/. The arXiv script makes outbound requests to export.arxiv.org and arxiv.org and downloads PDFs, which is disclosed but would benefit from explicit confirmation and size/content checks.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No install-time execution, package installation, or dependency fetching was found. The bundled shell wrapper contains unreachable embedded Python and fails shell syntax checking, which is a reliability issue rather than a security escalation.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The triggers are broad for paper and wiki workflows, and query/lint operations may write synthesis pages or logs; users should treat activation as write-capable, but the side effects are described in the skill text.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Persistence is limited to purpose-aligned local markdown/wiki content and downloaded PDFs. No credential access, privilege escalation, background service, scheduled task, or cross-session backdoor behavior was found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is building and maintaining a persistent research wiki; the instructions to ingest papers, update wiki pages, keep an index/log, and optionally search arXiv are coherent with that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you want an agent to maintain a persistent local research wiki and are comfortable with it creating or updating files under raw/ and wiki/. Run the bundled arXiv downloader only when you explicitly want recent PDFs saved locally, and review diffs or use version control because query and lint workflows can also persist new notes and log entries.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: Downgraded: arXiv paper search/download is explicitly documented in the Bundled Scripts section and fits the paper-ingestion workflow, though the frontmatter description is less specific.
[LP3] expected: Partly accepted as a guidance issue: the script uses network access and file writes without formal permission metadata, but the domains and default destination are visible and there is no hidden execution.
[SQP-1] expected: Partly accepted: triggers are broad enough for accidental write-capable activation, but they are centered on research notes, paper ingestion, wiki querying, and maintenance rather than unrelated tasks.
[SQP-2] expected: Downgraded: creating and updating raw/, wiki/, index, synthesis, and log files is the core disclosed behavior of a persistent wiki skill, not an unexpected side effect.
[SDI-1] expected: Downgraded: the arXiv behavior is not hidden; it is described in SKILL.md with usage, default count, destination, and filtering details.
[SDI-2] expected: Partly accepted as a hardening issue: remote PDFs are downloaded from hardcoded arXiv URLs without content-type or maximum-size validation, but they are not executed and the behavior is disclosed.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Accepted as a quality issue: the shell wrapper includes dead embedded Python after an exec line and fails bash syntax checking, but this does not add hidden capability.
[SQP-3] expected: Downgraded: the skill is clearly written for a Chinese research workflow; lack of bilingual docs may affect usability but is not a security concern by itself.
